claim: The structure checker is a dependency every node reader fails CLOSED without: when .hb/hb-lint.js is absent (an older bootstrapped project, a partial template copy), hb.js (every SHAPE_CHECKED verb, doctor, diagnose), hb-next-task.js, hb-report.js and hb-viz.js refuse with the same one-line 'dag.json could not be checked (hb-lint.js missing?)' class that gate.sh and tick.sh already emit — exit nonzero, no module-loader stack trace — on a lint-clean dag too, because a plan that cannot be checked is not known-sound. The policy is one across the node entry points: either every reader refuses this way or the phase's fail-closed claim has a hole shaped exactly like the file it depends on.
violation: In a bootstrapped mktemp project with a lint-clean dag and .hb/hb-lint.js removed: `node .hb/hb.js state` (or start/done/doctor), `node .hb/hb-next-task.js .hb/state.json`, `node .hb/hb-report.js .hb` or `node .hb/hb-viz.js .hb` prints a node:internal/modules/cjs/loader stack trace, exits 0, or proceeds to answer/append/dispatch unchecked — while gate.sh exits 4 and tick.sh wakes dag_corrupted for the same missing file.

claim: A dead resolver stays loud for as long as it is dead, on both runtimes, through every surface a driver reads: with hb-next-task.js missing or exiting nonzero (node) or resolver.resolve raising (python), EVERY tick — not only the first after .deadlock-alerted is cleared — is a wakeAgent:true human-needed signal carrying cause resolver_error, every exec run is a nonzero 'HB-EXEC STOP', and the signal carries a cure: data.action (the PROTOCOL deadlock text) and `diagnose deadlock` name resolver_error (the resolver script is missing/crashing — restore .hb/hb-next-task.js / the runtime) instead of only active_orphan and dag_invalid. The once-only deadlock flag may dedupe notifications, never the wake itself for this cause — the dag_corrupted path (which stops every run) is the model; r10 in tests/dag-shape.sh deletes .deadlock-alerted between its two checks and so never observes the second tick.
violation: On a fixture whose resolver persistently crashes or is missing: the second consecutive tick (no manual flag cleanup) returns wakeAgent:false (deadlock_waiting or any sleep) on either runtime; a second `hb-exec.js run` / `hb exec run` prints 'HB-EXEC IDLE: …' and exits 0; the deadlock wake's data.action or `diagnose deadlock` output is empty or names no cure for resolver_error; or the two runtimes disagree on the wake/sleep sequence.

claim: Refusal hygiene is total and runtime-identical: on a structurally malformed or unreadable dag, every refusing entry point — each mutating and read verb of hb.js and cli.py, hb-report.js, hb-viz.js, every gate.sh mode and `hb gate` mode — writes NOTHING to stdout, exactly one non-empty line to stderr, exits 1 (verbs, report, viz) or 4 (gate) with the same code on both runtimes for the same class, and leaves the ENTIRE .hb tree byte-identical (leases/, .*-alerted flags, state.json, .wlock, dag-view.html, the artifact/constraints files it was pointed at) — not merely events.jsonl and dag.json, which is all tests/dag-shape.sh r3 checksums. Only the resolver CLIs (`hb-next-task.js`, `hb next`) answer on stdout, with the deadlock JSON and exit 0, and the MCP tools with an isError result; a consumer that parses stdout (hb-exec's `hb('ready', N)`) must never see a refusal there.
violation: For some verb/mode on either runtime on a malformed dag: bytes on stdout, zero or more than one stderr line, an exit code other than 1 (verbs/report/viz) or 4 (gate) or one that differs from the twin runtime, or any file under .hb (or a side file such as dag-view.html or a lease) created, deleted or changed — e.g. `start t2` leaving a lease, `hb-viz.js` writing dag-view.html, `review … pass --artifact` touching the artifact store.

claim: The error payload is one list everywhere: for the same malformed dag, the errors carried by the tick wake (data.errors), the resolver deadlock (detail.errors), doctor's problems (minus the 'dag: ' prefix), MCP tick/next/lint/doctor and the first error of every refusal line are the STRUCTURE errors the runtime's lint reports, in lint order, capped identically (5) — byte-identical across node and python for the same dag (the parity case shape:tick compares only wakeAgent and reason, r1 only that errors is a non-empty list). The list is structure-only: a mutation that cascades into semantic errors (gates.G1 = "x" also yields '[P1] undefined gate: G1' in full lint) must not drag those into the payload on one runtime and not the other, and no surface may substitute a generic placeholder for the lint text.
violation: On any derived structure mutation or unreadable class: node tick data.errors != python tick data.errors (as JSON values); either differs from the structure-only errors `hb-lint.js --json` / `hb lint --json` report (first 5, lint order); a resolver's detail.errors or doctor's problem list disagrees with the tick's list on the same runtime; a refusal line's first error is not that list's first element; or a surface shows a generic text ('dag.json invalid') in place of the lint error.

claim: Fail-closed also reopens cleanly: the refusals and dag_corrupted wakes leave no residue that outlives the cure. After any number of refused verbs, gate attempts, exec runs and ticks on a malformed dag on BOTH runtimes, restoring dag.json to the lint-clean plan makes the very next tick next_task (same task) on node and python with no flag, lock or lease cleanup and no `rebuild`, doctor returns healthy exit 0 on both, and node and python `rebuild` produce identical projections (modulo last_updated) — the informational dag_corrupted events the node tick appends are inert to both projectors and never surface as a 'differs from the event-log' or unknown-event problem.
violation: After the refusals and the restore: a tick on either runtime sleeps (already_running, deadlock_waiting, no_pending_tasks) or wakes anything but next_task; doctor exits nonzero or lists a problem/note caused by the dag_corrupted events, a stale .lock/.wlock or a leftover lease; or the two rebuilds differ in anything but last_updated.

claim: An 'exempt' classification is a falsifiable claim — 'does not interpret the project's dag' — and tests/dag-shape.sh's PY_EXEMPT list makes it for `bench`, which does read it: bench.py copies dag.json into its scaffolded projects, runs the executor against them and scores the result from read_dag. On a structurally malformed or unreadable plan `hb bench` must therefore fail closed like a read verb — one stderr line naming the first structure error and `hb lint`, exit nonzero, no scorecard — and the class table must move it out of the exempt column (or the exemption must be made true by removing the dag read); every remaining exempt verb (init, protocol, refuters, mcp-serve) and MCP tool (code_context, code_discover, deplint) must be provably dag-free: identical output on the clean and the malformed fixture.
violation:
`HB_EXEC_BACKEND=script HB_EXEC_CMD='cat >/dev/null' hb bench --backend script --dir

` on a malformed dag exits 0 or prints a scorecard row ('esc yes' / 'done no') instead of the one-line refusal; or any verb/tool still classed exempt produces different output (or a refusal) on the malformed fixture than on the clean one.

claim: The MCP per-class table holds through every transport, not only the `_handle` function r8 calls directly: over stdio `serve` and over `serve_http` (POST JSON-RPC), on a malformed or unreadable dag, `initialize` and `tools/list` still succeed (the server stays reachable to deliver the refusal), tick returns the dag_corrupted wake with the errors and the PROTOCOL action (and no 'call tick again' nudge), next returns deadlock dag_invalid, lint/audit/doctor/diagnose report, the three dag-independent tools answer normally, and every other tool returns isError:true whose text is the same one-line refusal the CLI prints (first structure error + `hb lint`) — never a JSON-RPC protocol error, never a raise, never a tool result that looks like success.
violation: Through serve_http or stdio serve on a malformed dag: initialize or tools/list fails; a non-exempt act/read tool returns isError absent/false or a -32xxx protocol error; the tick result carries data.next ('call tick again') or lacks action/errors; the isError text omits the first structure error or `hb lint`; or any tool's result differs from the direct `_handle` result for the same call.
